title: SampleApp staging mentor 15m playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Goal: 15-minute guided mentor flow to get a developer from a sign-up link to a locally runnable SampleApp that calls Redwood hosted API, observes latency/cost telemetry, and practices one failover pattern. This is intentionally minimal: usable by a product advocate, an engineer doing office hours, or a partner SDR running a quick demo.

Audience: engineers familiar with Node or Python, first exposure to Redwood SDK, want a reproducible demo path and a few checks to verify production-like behavior.

Why this exists (context):
- We have a lot of long quickstarts; mentors need a tight, reliable flow for short sessions and interviews.
- Focus on observable outcomes: app responds, console shows token cost telemetry, and the app gracefully falls back to local stub when network removed.

Prep (for mentor, 3–5 minutes before session):
- Confirm the participant has: GitHub account or pastebin access, Node 18+/npm or Python 3.10+, and 2 terminal tabs.
- Create ephemeral API key (or use instructor key): scope=demo-hosted, expires=+1h. Put in clipboard.
- Start a staging instance of the sampleapp if you want to demo first: git fetch; ./scripts/start-staging.sh (optional).
- Open the telemetry dashboard quicklink for model "redwood-open/gpt-small-1" to show live latency/cost charts. Linked in artifacts.

Session script (15 minutes)
0:00–0:90 (Intro, 90s)
- One-line pitch: "We’ll go from repo clone to an instrumented sample app that calls Redwood in ~12 minutes and practice a failover."
- Confirm participant language preference (Node/Python) and paste ephemeral key into env.

0:90–6:00 (Get running, 3.5m)
- Commands (Node):
  - git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sampleapp.git && cd sampleapp
  - cp .env.example .env && EDITOR=. env <paste/replace with API key>
  - npm install && npm run dev
- Expected result: local server at http://localhost:3000 and a home page that accepts a prompt.
- Quick check: send a demo prompt ("Summarize this commit message: ...") and show response in UI.

6:00–9:00 (Instrument + telemetry, 3m)
- Show where SDK records token counts and latency: open /telemetry/agent (local console logs).
- Walk through the SDK call in code (lib/redwood-client.js or redwood.py): highlight options: model, max_tokens, stream, and fallback handler.
- Run a scripted request to show cost metadata: curl -X POST localhost:3000/generate -d '{"prompt":"short story: cat discovers key"}'
- Expected log output: "tokens_total=XX tokens_model=YY latency_ms=ZZ". If not, quick debugging checklist below.

9:00–12:00 (Failover drill, 3m)
- Explain concept: graceful degradation -> fallback to "local-stub" or reduced-cost model + cached prefix.
- Mentor toggles a simulated network failure (env var or local proxy): export REDWOOD_FORCE_FAIL=true (or use chrome devtools network offline).
- Participant triggers same prompt: observe fallback path in logs and UI shows cached response or local template.
- Expected: request doesn't crash; UI shows a short apology + cached result. Telemetry shows a fallback label.

12:00–14:00 (Quick prompt engineering + regression check, 2m)
- Show the small prompt test-suite in tests/prompt-smoke.json with 3 prompts used by CI. Run: npm run smoke.
- Emphasize how to add checkpoints to Redwood Optimize later (quick note).

14:00–15:00 (Wrap + next steps, 1m)
- Callouts: how to create an account project, where to find dedicated capacity docs, and link to deeper onboarding labs. Ask if they want a recorded link to the staging run.

Common problems + one-line fixes (mentor cheat sheet)
- Server won’t start: node logs show "Missing REDWOOD_API_KEY" -> ensure .env loaded, run "export REDWOOD_API_KEY=..." or use direnv.
- Empty responses/short truncation: check max_tokens and model selection; try model=redwood-open/gpt-medium-1 in .env.
- Telemetry not appearing: confirm TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true and that telemetry endpoint is reachable; tail local logs.
- Fallback didn't trigger: verify REDWOOD_FORCE_FAIL simulates network error; if using staging private deployment, confirm the routing policy is set to fallback on 5xx.

Mini debugging commands (copy/paste)
- Check API key: curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/whoami | jq
- Send a direct model call (Node): node -e "const c=require('./lib/redwood-client');c.generate('hi').then(console.log).catch(e=>console.error(e))"

Instrumentation notes (for mentor to highlight)
- Where token counts come from: SDK adds a small metadata header into responses (X-Redwood-Tokens). The sample app logs that to /telemetry/agent.
- Causal tracing: show request_id in UI footer; link it to Console -> Traces in Redwood Console (quick screenshot).

Acceptance criteria for a successful run (quick checks)
- Participant can start app and get a generation in <6 minutes.
- They can see a telemetry line showing tokens/latency.
- They can trigger the failover path and see a graceful message.

Extensions (if time remains or for follow-up)
- Swap to Dedicated pool: demo config change in .env to use DEDICATED_POOL_ID and show reduced variance on latency chart.
- Add a second-route A/B rollout: demonstrate canary to local dev environment.
- Quick embedding taste: run the small embedding example (scripts/embed-sample.sh) and show vector store size.

Open TODOs (for doc improvement)
- Add one-click ephemeral key generation link for mentors (ticket: DX-1150).
- Produce a single PNG cheat-sheet with commands + expected logs.
- Add Python snippets parity for a few of the copy/paste commands.

Notes to self (mentor)
- Keep this file in sync with sampleapp repo README; if telemetry path changes update the commands.
- Rehearse the fallback step — currently fragile with offline devtools in 2 browsers.

Quick copy-paste snippets (Node)
- .env example:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_demo_xxx
  REDWOOD_MODEL=redwood-open/gpt-small-1
  TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true
- Minimal generate example (JS):
  const Redwood = require('./lib/redwood-client');
  (async ()=>{
    const r = await Redwood.generate({prompt: 'todo: write a haiku'});
    console.log(r.text);
  })().catch(console.error);

If you find bugs while running this: leave a short note in the Slack thread (linked above) and file DX-1151 with repro steps.

End of scratchpad. Keep short, keep bulletable, keep it runnable.
